note: Why results/method_demo_synthetic.png cannot be compared byte-wise across machines. An earlier draft of this file attributed the difference to an unpinned numpy/scipy version; that was wrong and is corrected here.
finding: The committed PNG and a fresh render differ in 21,314 of 1,341,184 pixels (1.59%), and the difference is confined to the title and footer TEXT bands: 11,415 pixels in rows 0-149 and 9,899 in rows 750-831. Rows 150-749 -- the whole interior of both axes, i.e. every data pixel: the scene, the corridors and all six red candidate lines -- differ in exactly 0 pixels. Zero differing pixels are the candidate-line colour.
cause: Font rasterisation. The differing pixels are glyph edges, +/-218 grey levels on white and symmetric about zero (mean -0.04, std 69.9), which is what a different freetype build produces. matplotlib is 3.10.1 on both sides, at the same canvas (1612x832) and dpi, so this is below the level matplotlib pins.
not_a_dependency_problem: Verified, not assumed: make_scene(size=256, seed=1) yields the same float64 sha256 and extract_candidates yields the same six endpoints under numpy 2.1.3 / scipy 1.14.1 and numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1, and both environments render a byte-identical PNG to each other. The extractor imports only numpy and scipy.ndimage with no optional fallback, and analysis/pyproject.toml's open upper bounds are therefore not implicated in this figure.
consequence: PNG bytes are the wrong reproducibility gate for this figure. The numeric output is pinned instead in method_demo_synthetic.numeric.json and checked by analysis/tests/test_demo_reproducibility.py, so real drift in the scene or the extracted geometry fails on a number.
figure_left_unchanged: The committed PNG is correct and is not regenerated: every data pixel already matches what the committed code produces.

measurements.colorspace: all counts and statistics are the per-pixel max absolute difference over RGB channels; correlations are on the channel mean
